rationale: The same-gate MIN/SUB construction correctly isolates the accrual-complexity ranking within distressed firms and is a legitimate extension of the earlier single-channel ABS(aoloch) test, though gross absolute accrual magnitude is close to published accrual-quality/opacity measures and coverage will be thin because all four cash-flow items are required.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived PayablesAdjustedCashFragility — the only changes are moving the debt term from the conditioning gate into the scaling denominator and dropping one gate component — so it cannot diagnose why that signal's cross-sectional and portfolio evidence diverged.

The ratio |dpc|/(|dpc|+|non-dep gap|) is arithmetically one minus the archived NonDepAccrualDominanceUnderDebt ratio (dp vs dpc are near-identical) under the identical gate, so this is a mechanical sign inversion of an already-evaluated signal rather than a new test.

The sign convention and gate logic are internally consistent, but the base leg is essentially the classic working-capital accruals anomaly (Sloan) with a distress conditioner, and it overlaps heavily with the archived inventory/receivable-buildup-under-distress constructions.

The denominator is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis — ABS(re) means a large retained-earnings deficit (a thin cushion) inflates the denominator and shrinks the signal, and re is largely double-counted inside ceq — while the signal itself is a univariate scaled-accrual ratio with no real cross-theme interaction and near-duplicates archived OpaqueAccrualFragility.

Gross-minus-net absolute accrual activity is a genuinely novel "offsetting channel churn" construct with a coherent classification-shifting/cash-conversion story and a correctly implemented conditional gate, though it will be highly correlated with the companion gross-magnitude proposal and coverage is likely low.
